NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.
Article Summary: NCP leader Praful Patel visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups. The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar's leadership.

NEW DELHI: Is a storm brewing in Maharashtra’s Pawar clan? The family that saw a vertical split in 2023, seems to be at a crossroads again."As a member of the Pawar family and their relative, I want to alert Parth Pawar, Jay Pawar and Sunetra. They need to understand the political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them": Nephew Rohit Rajendra Pawar’s warning for his “” Sunetra Pawar, who is the wife of late Ajit Pawar , and her two children.Sunetra, who is the deputy chief minister in the ruling BJP-led Mahayuti at present, is on the other side of the family divide. She and her sons control the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), which was originally formed by Sharad Pawar in 1999 but was wrested from him by Ajit Pawar in 2023.So, let’s look at some of the recent developments to analyse if Rohit Pawar ’s warning has a genuine basis.Senior NCP leaders met Union home minister Amit Shah recently. Some reports suggested that the NCP leaders complained to Amit Shah about the unilateral functioning of party MP Parth Pawar and a lack of proper coordination. The NCP spokesperson denied this claim and slammed irresponsible media reporting.NCP chief Sunetra Pawar convened an urgent meeting of the core committee at her official residence, Devgiri. This was the second meeting of the core committee in a week. The first meeting happened after the senior leaders had met Amit Shah.At the core committee meeting, the party legislators and ministers expressed serious concerns over internal frictions and claimed the party is weakening in the absence of unity.Also read: Miffed with Parth, NCP seniors eager to revive merger talks with Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP); surprised, says Rohit When Sharad Pawar was hospitalised, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called him in the hospital and requested the veteran politician to prioritise his health and rest. PM Modi’s message to the senior Pawar, "Supriya and we will handle the country. You take care of your health and rest. Let your blessings remain with us," sparked political buzz. And perhaps carried a political undertone about possible churn, amid speculation about Sunetra Pawar and her sons' political future.Adding fuel to the fire, Union minister and Republican Party of India (Athawale) president Ramdas Athawale claimed that Sule could be considered for a position in the Union cabinet during its next expansion if she joined the ruling NDA.These four developments, significant in their own ways, collectively point to the flux within the NCP factions after the party was split in 2023.Ajit Pawar, while he was alive, had managed a firm grip on his faction winning 41 assembly seats in the 2024 assembly elections. There were even talks of the two factions uniting again. However, his unfortunate death in a helicopter crash in January 2026, suddenly made the NCP vulnerable and the merger talks were put to rest.Ajit’s wife Sunetra Pawar, who took over the reins of the NCP and also became a minister in the Mahayuti government, tried to fill the vacuum in the party.Her sons - Parth and Jay Pawar - became an integral part of decision-making. Senior NCP leaders who had worked with Ajit Pawar over the years were sidelined. This led to heartburn and talks of discontent within the party. It is in this context that the meeting of senior NCP leaders with Amit Shah and the subsequent meeting of the party’s core committee held by Sunetra Pawar have set tongues wagging.Rohit Pawar in his warning message had pointed to the “political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them.” So, is something happening behind the scenes? Is the BJP working to merge the NCP factions to water down the influence of Sunetra and her sons?Well, there is no definitive answer to these questions.For the record, the NCP has denied all speculations of any power tussle within the party.NCP spokesperson Umesh Patil termed the reports suggesting senior party functionaries met Shah, a BJP leader, in New Delhi three days ago without informing Sunetra Pawar as "completely incorrect".Patil maintained she herself had requested the Union minister to give time to a delegation of senior party leaders. He said Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth had met Shah twice last month when discussions were held on matters related to the party, a BJP ally and constituent of the Mahayuti government in the state.Sunetra Pawar had then requested Shah to meet senior NCP leaders who had been involved in discussions with BJP leaders when the party joined the NDA, said Patil.An appointment with Shah for the delegation was subsequently given, said the spokesperson, adding the NCP's core committee and legislative wing meetings were also scheduled several days in advance.The official spokesperson also defended the involvement of Parth Pawar in party affairs, saying the Pawar family had dedicated itself to the organisation following the death of former NCP president Ajit Pawar in an air crash in January this year."After Ajit Dada's death, Sunetra Pawar (and her sons) Parth and Jay have dedicated themselves to the party," Umesh Patil said.Now, coming to the second aspect of the developments. It is not for the first time that the Prime Minister has expressed his special bond with Sharad Pawar, despite the two leaders being on opposite sides of the political divide.In July this year, Sharad Pawar and Supriya Sule met the Prime Minister at his office even as opposition MPs protested outside. The Prime Minister was then seen receiving Pawar at the door of his room. During the meeting Sharad Pawar submitted a memorandum to the Prime Minister listing the issues faced by the farmers in the country and issues related to irrigation.In February 2025, PM Modi made a gesture of respect by helping 84-year-old Sharad Pawar with his chair on stage and offering him a glass of water.In August 2023, Sharad Pawar shared the stage with PM Modi in Pune when the Prime Minister was conferred with the Lokmanya Tilak Award. The move created unease among some members of the opposition INDIA alliance. Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) questioned the optics of the two leaders appearing together, especially when Sharad Pawar was a key leader of the opposition’s INDIA bloc.Well, the saffron party is obviously not ‘working’ or ‘not working’ to facilitate a '' reconciliation moment for the Pawar clan. The real prize of the BJP would be co-opting the political infrastructure of the veteran, who was also known as '' (people's king). With decades of work, the influence of Pawar Saheb extends beyond assembly seats to an entrenched network of sugar cooperatives, district banks, local bodies and influential political families across western Maharashtra. Though the seats and power is not transferable as it is, a working understanding with Sharad Pawar could give the BJP access to this ecosystem without having to build its own grassroots machinery from scratch.If Sharad Pawar does decide to merge and if Athawale’s claim turns out to be true, Sule may get an opportunity to be in “power” again.There may also be a larger opposition calculation at play. Sharad Pawar was instrumental in stitching together the Maha Vikas Aghadi and managing the competing ambitions of the Congress and Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena. Any rapprochement with the BJP, even without a formal merger, could weaken this arrangement, complicate seat-sharing and disrupt opposition coordination in Maharashtra. The BJP could gain not just an ally but also greater room to manoeuvre against a much fragmented opposition.This will also help the BJP in Maharashtra to keep the Eknath Shinde Shiv Sena in check. The recent loss of the ruling Mahayuti in the MLC elections turned into an ugly war of words between the two allies - with the BJP accusing the Shinde Sena of not working for the coalition.A united NCP on its side may perhaps provide the BJP manoeuvring room against the Shinde Sena in Maharashtra.
Article Summary: Nephew Rohit Rajendra Pawar has warned his family about the political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them. Sunetra Pawar, who is the wife of late Ajit Pawar and her two children, is on the other side of the family divide. She and her sons control the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), which was originally formed by Sharad Pawar in 1999.

CHENNAI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has asked the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, which is slated for release on Nov 20.The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions, then asks how long people will tolerate this. The teaser then shows him assaulting doctors and nursing staff members inside a hospital, which the IMA says is presented as a heroic and justified act.In a representation dated Nov 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak urged the board to deny certification under Section 4(2)(v) read with Section 5B(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and the 2026 certification guidelines.The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.It has sought a screening under Section 7C for IMA representatives, the presence of an IMA-nominated medical expert when the examining committee views the film, and a hearing before any decision is taken.It said if any certificate is recommended, the chairperson should refer the film to a revising committee under Rule 25(1) of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024. It wants every scene showing violence against healthcare workers as justified or heroic deleted, along with the dialogue on corruption. It also wants a prominent disclaimer that the film does not represent the medical profession and that such violence is punishable.The association asked for a written, reasoned decision and priority consideration given the release date. It reserved the right to approach the courts.
Article Summary: The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions. The teaser then shows him assaulting doctors and nursing staff members inside a hospital. The IMA says is presented as a heroic and justified act.

NEW DELHI: Observing that the Constitution is supreme and that no individual or political organisation stands above it, Supreme Court Friday issued notice to office-bearers of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC), including its president, seeking their response on why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them over a now-deleted social media post on CJI Surya Kant.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi was hearing a petition filed by advocate Vineet Jindal seeking suo motu action regarding the post published on the official X account of Indian National Congress's Keralam unit.KPCC submitted that the post was uploaded without office-bearers' approval, and was immediately taken down after it came to the notice of the party. It said an unconditional apology had also been issued.The bench, however, said SC would examine "whether it has come from the pen or your heart" and agreed to hear the petition. "...Independence of the judiciary is not a matter of political convenience," the court said.It said while judgements are always open to criticism, "freedom of expression cannot be a shield for intimidation or interference with the administration of justice" and "judicial restraint must never be mistaken for institutional weakness".
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues notice to office-bearers of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee. It is seeking their response on why contempt proceedings should not be initiated against them over a now-deleted social media post on CJI Surya Kant. The post was published on the official X account of Indian National Congress's Keralam unit.

NEW DELHI: The death of tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat, who allegedly died by suicide at her Ranchi residence on Friday, has triggered a political storm in Jharkhand. Opposition parties have accused the Hemant Soren-led government and police administration of failing to protect her despite repeated complaints of harassment. The controversy has intensified following an emotional Facebook Live broadcast in which Bhagat, visibly distressed and in tears, accused land brokers and people associated with the government of harassing her. She also alleged that her attempts to seek protection from the authorities had gone unanswered.In the nearly 11-minute video, which was viewed by thousands, Bhagat spoke about the threats she allegedly faced, apologised to her parents and expressed despair over her inability to fight the administration. Her death has prompted the BJP to demand a CBI investigation and chief minister Hemant Soren's resignation. The CPI(ML) Liberation, an ally of the ruling government, has also called for a fair investigation, while tribal organisations and local leaders have demanded accountability.The Soren govt responded to BJP's allegation admitting that though Bhagat was critical of the JMM govt she was not an "enemy"."Several land mafias and land brokers are BJP office-bearers, including prominent leaders.She may have criticised our party and government, but she was not our enemy. She was an Adivasi daughter of Jharkhand. The circumstances that led her to take this extreme step must be investigated. Police should examine her CDR details and the post-mortem report. Our police are conducting an impartial investigation, and action will be taken against whoever is found guilty. Let the preliminary police report come in the next two to four days," JMM central spokesperson Manoj Pandey said.The incident has particularly angered tribal communities, with members planning a symbolic protest ahead of her last rites at her ancestral village Uru in Gumla district on Saturday.In her final Facebook Live broadcast, Bhagat alleged that speaking out against the state government and land brokers could put people's lives at risk. She also claimed that despite repeatedly approaching the police and seeking security, she had received no meaningful assistance."I should have understood this earlier... People say there is BJP, there is Congress, but there is no one... My parents will be deeply hurt. My father played his role in the Jharkhand agitation. I tried very hard to fight the administration and also tried to talk to them about security... But today I have to embrace my own death because this Hemant Soren government can humiliate women, and I cannot bear this," she said.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto said Bhagat had approached several people, including police officers, political representatives and social organisations, for help. He called for a comprehensive CBI investigation to establish whether complaints were ignored and identify those responsible.Her father, Handu Bhagat, also demanded a central investigation, alleging that influential people were involved. "I demand a high-level inquiry into my daughter's death. The probe should be conducted by the CBI, because high-profile people are involved," he told reporters.Ranchi Rural SP Gaurav Goswami said an Unnatural Death (UD) case had been registered and that forensic evidence had been collected from her residence. A medical board conducted the post-mortem examination."Everything is currently under investigation. We are looking into every point you have raised; however, it would be inappropriate to comment on any specific detail before the investigation is complete. Once the investigation concludes, all findings will be shared with you," Goswami said, responding to allegations of police negligence.Nisha Kumari Bhagat was a tribal activist from Jharkhand who had raised her voice against alleged injustice, starvation, religious conversion and land grabbing. She was particularly vocal against land brokers and what she described as harassment of tribal communities.According to Jharkhand BJP president Aditya Sahu, Bhagat had consistently spoken against exploitation and oppression but received no support from the government. He questioned why the police had failed to intervene despite thousands watching her distress broadcast.Union minister of state for Defence Sanjay Seth also accused the state administration of failing to act, demanding the arrest of the Pithoria police station officer-in-charge, whom Bhagat had allegedly accused of ignoring her complaints."The death of Nisha by suicide is a grim reflection of the crumbling law and order situation in Jharkhand," Seth said, reiterating the demand for a CBI probe.The case shares an eerie similarity to the killing of Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, whose death in a controversial police encounter in Bihar has sparked widespread outrage. A video apparently showing the 28-year-old activist throwing away his pistol moments before being shot has raised allegations that he was killed after surrendering. Amid mounting political pressure, the Bihar government had ordered a judicial inquiry led by a retired High Court judge and suspended four police personnel pending investigation.
Article Summary: Tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat, who allegedly died by suicide, has triggered a political storm in Jharkhand. Article Title: '1,800 fake AI books, inflated prices': Periyar library pits CM Vijay against DMK
Article Text:
Vijay accused the DMK of turning the institution into what he described as a centre of corruption.

What are the allegations against DMK

Vijay calls DMK 'fountainhead of corruption'

Stalin defends the project

Udhayanidhi targets CM Vijay

Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday accused the previous DMK government of corruption in the purchase of books for Coimbatore's Periyar Knowledge World, days after allegations emerged that nearly 1,800 fake AI-generated books had been bought at inflated prices.Vijay credited writer and professor Perumal Murugan with exposing the alleged irregularities and said he deserved to be commended.The controversy has also drawn in the Congress, with state party president Manickam Tagore demanding a comprehensive probe into the purchases. The demand puts the DMK, the Congress's former ally, under pressure to answer allegations of wrongdoing during its tenure.The DMK, meanwhile, has accused the Vijay government of trying to take credit for a project built under its rule and covering up the name of its 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme at the newly inaugurated centre.The controversy centres on the purchase of books for Periyar Knowledge World, also known as Periyar Arivulagam, a library and science centre in Coimbatore.Writer Perumal Murugan reportedly flagged alleged irregularities in the procurement process. Citing his allegations, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore claimed that nearly 1,800 fake, AI-generated books from Agalvilakku Pathippagam were purchased at inflated prices.He also alleged that the books carried fabricated author and publisher details.In a letter to Vijay, Tagore sought a comprehensive investigation into the alleged multi-crore corruption. He demanded that the disputed books be removed, those responsible identified and arrested, and similar purchases at other state-run libraries examined.The Congress leader's intervention is politically significant because the allegations concern the previous DMK government, with which the Congress was previously allied. His demand puts the spotlight on the DMK's record in office even as the party faces attacks from the ruling TVK.Vijay seized on the allegations to launch a sharp attack on the DMK, accusing it of turning the institution into what he described as a centre of corruption.Hitting out at the opposition party, the chief minister called it the "fountainhead of corruption" and alleged that its claims of building the institution after careful scrutiny had been undermined by the book procurement controversy."The DMK has engaged in corruption in a slightly different way, turning Coimbatore Periyar Knowledge World itself into a world of corruption," the ruling TVK founder alleged in a statement.He further claimed that the DMK had a history of corruption, including in the awarding of tenders, and said the party would not be forgiven by future generations of Tamil Nadu."That the DMK is a party which built a very huge world of corruption for themselves is getting exposed one after the other," he alleged.Vijay's remarks came on the day he inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam, which houses a library, a digital library and a planetarium.The DMK has sought to highlight the institution as a major project completed under its 'Dravidian Model' government.Party president and former chief minister M K Stalin visited the centre on Wednesday along with Dravidar Kazhagam president K Veeramani. He expressed satisfaction over its completion and urged students and young people to visit the facility to understand the principles and ideals of the Dravidian movement and Periyar.Stalin said nearly 99.75% of the work had been completed and suggested that the project could have been abandoned had it been left unfinished."Fortunately, the Periyar Knowledge Centre has reached the stage of near completion. Had the project been left halfway, the current govt would have dropped the project and had brought it to a closure. Thankfully, it has escaped that fate," he remarked.He also expressed hope that other library projects would be completed and opened to the public, saying such institutions could encourage reading and help younger generations understand Tamil Nadu's social reform movements.The DMK's criticism of the Vijay government has also focused on an alleged attempt to remove the previous regime's imprint from the institution.Leader of Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin welcomed the inauguration of the centre but alleged that the name of the DMK government's 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme had been covered up at the premises.In a post on X, Udhayanidhi said the facility had been built at a cost of Rs 290 crore under the previous government's 'Dravidian Model' and accused the TVK of taking credit for projects initiated by the DMK."Those who habitually 'stick their own labels' (take credit) on the schemes of our government have, this time, gone as far as covering up the name 'Naan Mudhalvan' (I am the First/Leader) at the Periyar Knowledge World. In this regime—led by a 'cheap' chief minister obsessed with sticking his own labels—what is the reason for not only undermining the 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme but also refusing to even accept its name?" he said.Questioning the alleged move, Udhayanidhi asked whether the word 'Mudhalvan' reminded the ruling party only of the DMK's leadership, or whether it did not want students to become leaders and top achievers."Instead of running a 'circus'—by covering up names given by our government, cancelling schemes, and then performing U-turns by 'cancelling the cancellations'—this 'dummy' chief minister should focus on governing in the interest of the people."The row has thus developed into a wider political contest over alleged corruption in the previous regime, the ownership of a high-profile public project and the legacy each party wants to claim from it. While the Congress is seeking an investigation into the alleged book purchases, Vijay has used the allegations to target the DMK, which is accusing his government of erasing its contribution to the institution.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay accused the previous DMK government of corruption in the purchase of books for Coimbatore's Periyar Knowledge World. Vijay credited writer and professor Perumal Murugan with exposing the alleged irregularities and said he deserved to be commended. The controversy has also drawn in the Congress, with state party president Manickam Tagore demanding a comprehensive probe into the purchases.

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat was found dead at her residence in Ranchi on Friday, hours after allegedly going live on Facebook and speaking about threats she faced for raising her voice against the Jharkhand government and alleged land brokers.Police suspect suicide, though the exact circumstances surrounding her death are yet to be established, according to the news agency PTI.In the nearly 11-minute video, which was available on her Facebook profile, Bhagat is seen crying and alleging that speaking out against the "Hemant Soren government and its land brokers meant inviting death".The video ends abruptly, with the camera apparently getting blocked by a green object.Ranchi City Superintendent of Police Paras Rana told PTI that Bhagat's body was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a room at her house. Article Title: Telangana student pursuing master's at UMass goes missing in Boston, last seen leaving home for a walk
Article Text:
Sreeja Reddy Koya, a 23-year-old student from Nalgonda, is missing in Boston after taking a walk.





HYDERABAD: A 23-year-old student from Nalgonda district, who is pursuing her master’s degree at the University of Massachusetts (UMass) in the US, has gone missing in Boston. According to local police, Sreeja Reddy Koya was last seen leaving her residence in Dorchester, near Edison Green, at around 9.45 pm on Nov 2 for an evening walk.The incident came to light after her friends alerted the police when she failed to return from the walk. Her phone's location reportedly indicated an area near a beach, but her whereabouts remain unknown.The Boston Police Department has issued a missing-person alert, seeking the public's assistance in tracing Sreeja. According to the alert, she may be in the vicinity of Carson Beach or Harbor Point.“The Boston Police Department is actively working to locate Sreeja Koya and urges anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to call 911,” a notice on the department's website stated.The University of Massachusetts has also made an appeal on social media, seeking information about its missing student.According to the university’s notice, “Koya was seen wearing a black jacket, grey jeans and no shoes.” The notice further stated that she “may be experiencing a mental health crisis and is known to frequent the Carson Beach and Harbor Point areas”.Sreeja is the daughter of Koya Yadagiri Reddy and Roopa, residents of Shabdullapuram village in Kanagal mandal of Nalgonda district.She moved to the US in 2025 to pursue a MS degree and is expected to complete the course in about six months, according to sources. Her parents are worried and anxiously awaiting information about their daughter’s whereabouts.Local media reports said Sreeja had attended classes on the day she went missing, completed her part-time job and returned to her accommodation, which she shares with other Telugu students.Roads and buildings minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy has urged the Indian embassy, the ministry of external affairs (MEA), Boston police and other officials concerned to coordinate their efforts and ensure that Sreeja is traced safely. Meanwhile, Krishna Prasad of the Telugu Association of North America (TANA) said the organisation was coordinating with local officials, Sreeja’s friends and others to help trace her.

Her phone's location indicated an area near a beach, but her whereabouts remain unknown.

Article Title: Inside Bengaluru's house of horrors: Mutton curry invite, sleeping pills, TV at full blast, bodies in gunny bags
Article Text:
S Indushekhar reportedly killed his wife Sunitha and six of her relatives at their rented house

Gold ornaments removed before bodies were dumped

10-year-old boy was next target

Nearly 20 years of marital discord behind killings

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most shocking element of this case? The number of victims. The involvement of a minor. The use of deception to lure victims. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: A dinner invitation, sleeping pills and a television blaring at full volume allegedly formed part of a chilling sequence of events leading to seven murders at a rented house in Rajajinagar.Police suspect that a 52-year-old cab driver, S Indushekhar, killed his wife and six members of her extended family over a 15-day period before wrapping their bodies in plastic sheets, stuffing them into gunny bags and ferrying them in his car to different locations.The latest development in the case came with the recovery of the bodies of Indushekhar's wife Sunitha and her mother Rupavathi from a forest area in Salem district of Tamil Nadu. This has taken the total number of bodies recovered to three. A 12-member team comprising family members has travelled to Salem to identify the bodies and complete the necessary legal formalities.According to cops, Indushekhar allegedly killed Sunitha on the night of October 14. The following day, his 17-year-old daughter called Rupavathi and invited her to their home for dinner, saying they would prepare mutton curry.Investigators suspect the invitation was part of a plan to lure her to the house, where she was allegedly killed.During interrogation, Indushekhar allegedly told police that he used sleeping pills to sedate his victims before bludgeoning them with a grindstone after they fell asleep. He would turn up the television volume while attacking them to ensure that neighbours did not hear the sounds of the assaults, police said.After the killings, Indushekhar and his daughter allegedly wrapped the bodies in multiple layers of plastic sheets to prevent blood from leaking out before placing them in gunny bags. They would then carry the bags to his Toyota Etios in the early hours and drive away to dispose of the bodies at different locations.Police have recovered at least half a dozen perfume bottles from the Toyota Etios, which is now part of the investigation. Investigators are examining their possible use in connection with the disposal of the bodies.Also read: Bengaluru family massacre: Accused's daughter 'assisted' him at every stage of killings, say cops Investigators have also found that Indushekhar allegedly removed gold ornaments from the bodies of his wife and three other women before disposing of them. He is suspected to have sold some of the jewellery, and police are now trying to trace the transactions and establish where the ornaments went.The postmortem report of seven-year-old Puneeth, who was allegedly killed on October 29, confirmed four blunt-force injuries to his head, including the forehead and crown, police said.The 52-year-old cab driver was arrested near Ulsoorgate on Wednesday. Police suspect he killed seven people at his rented house on 59th Cross, Rajajinagar V Block, between October 14 and 31. The victims included his wife and six members of her extended family.His 17-year-old daughter is suspected to have assisted him in some of the murders and in disposing of the bodies. Investigators are probing her alleged role in the sequence of killings and the subsequent disposal of the victims.A 10-year-old boy, the son of two of the victims, was found in Indushekhar's car when police arrested him near Ulsoorgate. Investigators said the accused had allegedly planned to kill the child as well.The boy had reportedly been taken away from his home on the pretext that his parents had gone on a pilgrimage. He spent several days with Indushekhar and his daughter, unaware that his parents had allegedly been murdered. Police suspect that the accused was waiting for an opportunity to kill him before his arrest.The boy's presence in the car proved crucial in the investigation, with police rescuing him before the alleged plan could be carried out.Police suspect the murders stemmed from a prolonged marital dispute between Indushekhar and Sunitha. During questioning, he allegedly told investigators that he had been in conflict with his wife for nearly 20 years and blamed her relatives for supporting her during their disputes.Investigators are also examining the family property angle. Relatives of the victims have alleged that a dispute over property worth around Rs 3 crore could have been behind the killings, though police are continuing to establish the motive.The case came to light after family members grew suspicious when several relatives went missing. A relative had also noticed that messages were being sent from Sunitha's phone, but nobody was receiving calls from her.Investigators suspect Indushekhar had been using his wife's phone to message her mother and conceal her murder.Police are continuing to investigate the circumstances of all seven murders, the disposal of the bodies at different locations, the suspected sale of gold ornaments and the role of the accused's daughter.
Article Summary: S Indushekhar, 52, allegedly killed his wife and six members of her extended family over a 15-day period. His 17-year-old daughter is suspected to have assisted him in some of the murders and in disposing of the bodies. Police suspect the killings stemmed from a prolonged marital dispute.

Article Title: In Faridabad for nephew's wedding, ex-Tech Mahindra regional business head shot dead by neighbour over parking dispute; fired 15 rounds

FARIDABAD: A man was shot dead following a dispute over vehicle parking in Sector 21C, Faridabad, on the night of Dhanteras, two days before Diwali.The deceased, identified as Paramjeet Dhankar, was allegedly shot by his neighbour, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who opened fire with his licensed pistol.According to his LinkedIn profile, Dhankar had previously served as the regional business head of Tech Mahindra’s Asia-Pacific region.He was based in Singapore and was currently working as the senior vice-president of FPT Software Company Limited.According to police, the accused fired around 15-16 rounds, of which three to four bullets hit Paramjeet, killing him on the spot.Paramjeet lived on the first floor of house number 641 with his wife, son and daughter. He was employed with a private company in Singapore.He had returned to Faridabad just two days before the incident to attend his nephew's wedding, scheduled for November 24. He originally belonged to Hisar.Police said Paramjeet had returned home from the gym around 8pm when an argument broke out between him and Mohan, who lived on the third floor of the same building, over vehicle parking. Police are also investigating whether the dispute was linked to a pet dog.The argument escalated, following which the accused allegedly opened fire at Paramjeet.According to police, the two families had a history of disputes. Five days before the incident, the accused had allegedly abused Paramjeet's son.After the shooting, Mohan fled with his family. On receiving information, teams from the local police, crime branch and forensic science laboratory (FSL) reached the spot. Empty cartridges were recovered from the crime scene.Police are searching for the accused.Prahlad Kumar, SHO of Surajkund police station, confirmed the incident and said teams were investigating the case and searching for the accused.He said the accused had fired around 15 rounds.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Paramjeet Dhankar. He was shot by his neighbour, Mohan alias Monu Sharma, who opened fire with his licensed pistol. According to police, the two families had a history of disputes. Five days before the incident, the accused had allegedly abusedParamjeet's son.

Article Title: Two years after Donald Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts over a $130,000 payment to Stormy Daniels, his lawyers ask a New York appeals court to overturn the verdict on immunity and legal grounds
Article Text:
Trump's lawyers questioned jury unanimity requirements, while prosecutors highlighted the defence's earlier acceptance of the judge's instructions.

Lawyers challenge the legal foundation of the conviction

Presidential immunity becomes another battleground

Judges question both sides as Trump continues his fight

US President Donald Trump is once again under judicial scrutiny. Nearly two years after a New York jury found him guilty of 34 felony counts connected to a hush money payment made before the 2016 presidential election, Trump's legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and the evidence presented during his trial.According to AP News, Trump's attorneys appeared before a New York appellate court on Thursday, November 5, arguing that the conviction should be overturned because the prosecution relied on federal election law to elevate the charges from misdemeanours to felonies.The case originated from a $130,000 payment made by Trump's former lawyer and fixer, Michael Cohen, to adult film performer Stormy Daniels shortly before the 2016 election. The payment was intended to secure her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump approximately a decade earlier, which the president has consistently denied.Cohen was subsequently reimbursed by Trump's company in 2017, with the payments recorded as legal expenses.Prosecutors argued that the business records were deliberately falsified to conceal an alleged conspiracy to influence the election.Trump's lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr. maintained that Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg's office had improperly relied on the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), arguing that federal election law could not form the basis of a state prosecution.CBS News reported that the defence also challenged the jury instructions, arguing that jurors should have been required to unanimously agree on the underlying crime that elevated the falsification charges to felonies.Another significant aspect of the appeal concerns evidence from Trump's first presidential term. His legal team argued that testimony involving former White House communications director Hope Hicks and Trump's social media posts should not have been presented to jurors because they involved official presidential conduct protected by immunity.Hicks had testified about discussions with Trump after the Daniels allegations became public in 2018. His lawyers maintained that the conversations concerned his responsibilities as president, including managing press inquiries.However, prosecutors disputed that interpretation. According to AP News, Steven Wu, representing Bragg's office, argued that the conversations reflected Trump's personal opinions rather than official presidential duties.The prosecution also maintained that even if certain evidence should have been excluded, its admission did not affect the overall outcome because substantial other evidence supported the conviction.The five-judge panel repeatedly interrupted both legal teams with questions about their arguments. One judge also questioned whether the cumulative admission of potentially improper evidence could still be considered harmless.CBS News noted that Trump's defence additionally challenged the requirement for jury unanimity on the underlying offences, while prosecutors pointed out that the trial defence had previously accepted the judge's approach.The May 2024 conviction followed a unanimous jury verdict. Trump was found guilty on all 34 counts but received no punishment that impeded his return to the White House.His attempts to shift the case from state to federal court meanwhile have also faced setbacks.A federal judge denied his immunity dismissal request for the third time in August, with another appeal scheduled for Nov. 16.The New York appeals court has not announced its decision, leaving Trump's historic conviction in limbo.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram
Article Summary: Donald Trump was found guilty of 34 felony counts in May 2024. His legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and evidence presented during his trial.

Article Title: In 2022, two Michigan brothers became embroiled in a land dispute after one ploughed a landscaped strip beside the other's home; four years later, an appeals court revived the boundary claim after a $
Article Text:
A Michigan appeals court revived a couple's claim over a 0.13-acre strip their family had maintained for years. (AI image)

Why the trial court rejected the land claim

Why the appeals court revived the claim

Appeals court rejects other challenges

In 2022, a Michigan man ploughed a landscaped strip of land beside his brother's home, triggering a dispute over who had the right to use it. Frederick G. Bender and his wife, Susan, said their family had maintained the 0.13-acre area for years, although it was part of his brother David A. Bender's property. They sued David and his wife, Jean, seeking compensation and recognition of their claim over the land. Four years later, an appeals court revived their boundary claim after a lower court rejected it, while awarding them $5,364.44 for the damage caused.According to court records , Frederick and Susan had maintained the disputed strip for several years. The practice reportedly went back to a time when one of Frederick's parents owned their property. They argued that David and Jean had accepted this arrangement over the years and that the boundary should be recognised in their favour.The disputed area measured 0.13 acres and lay along the northern and eastern edges of Frederick and Susan's property. Both boundaries were surrounded by land belonging to David and Jean. In August and September 2022, David and Jean ploughed the disputed area. They also damaged a separate strip belonging to Frederick and Susan.The couple then filed a lawsuit seeking compensation for the damage and recognition of their claim over the disputed land. David and Jean, however, argued that they had continued to use the area themselves. They said they had occupied it and used it to enter and leave their property.The case also involved a 1991 foreclosure ruling concerning the property. David and Jean relied on that earlier decision to argue that Frederick and Susan could not make a fresh claim over the disputed area. The trial court accepted their argument and rejected the boundary claim. However, the Michigan Court of Appeals later found that the earlier case had dealt with a different issue.The 1991 case concerned the foreclosure of the property. Its order stated that certain claims over the mortgaged land would be barred after the sale if the property was not redeemed within six months.One of the defendants in that earlier case was the father of one of the plaintiffs in the present dispute. David and Jean relied on the wording of the old judgment to challenge Frederick and Susan's claim.The trial court agreed with them and held that the earlier ruling prevented the couple from seeking recognition of the disputed boundary.However, the trial court allowed their claims over the damage to proceed. David and Jean did not appear at the trial. Frederick and Susan won those claims and were awarded $5,364.44 for trespass and waste.The couple challenged the rejection of their boundary claim before the Michigan Court of Appeals. They argued that the 1991 case had never decided where the boundary between the two properties should be.The appeals court agreed with Frederick and Susan on this issue. It found that the earlier foreclosure case and the present dispute dealt with different questions.The 1991 case concerned the foreclosure of the property and the rights of people seeking to recover it. The present dispute, however, was about whether David and Jean had accepted a different property boundary because Frederick's family had maintained the disputed strip for years.The judges noted that the earlier case had never examined whether David and Jean had accepted the boundary claimed by Frederick and Susan. Therefore, its ruling could not automatically prevent the couple from making a fresh claim.The court said the wording of the 1991 judgment did not stop an owner of neighbouring land from asking for recognition of a boundary based on how the land had been used over time.The judges also clarified that the earlier ruling did not necessarily give Frederick and Susan the right to recover the disputed land through the foreclosure proceedings. Their present claim was based on a separate argument about the boundary.The appeals court concluded that the trial court had wrongly rejected the claim by relying on the 1991 judgment. It set aside that part of the decision and sent the case back for further proceedings.Frederick and Susan had also challenged the trial court's decision to cancel an earlier default against David and Jean.The defendants had initially failed to respond to the lawsuit within the required time. A default was entered against them on March 14, 2023. They later asked the court to cancel it, explaining why they had missed the deadline.The trial court accepted their explanation. It considered their medical problems, the time needed to find documents and their apparent misunderstanding about the response deadline. It also found that they had a possible defence because they claimed to have continued using the disputed land.The appeals court found no reason to overturn that decision. It noted that the defendants had responded within 14 days after the deadline and had promptly asked the court to cancel the default.The couple also argued that David and Jean should have faced a default judgment for failing to answer formal questions sent to them during the case.The appeals court rejected this argument as well. It said the court rules did not allow a default judgment simply because someone failed to answer such questions. Instead, unanswered requests could be treated as accepted. The judges found no reason to interfere with the lower court's decisions on these issues.The appeals court ultimately revived the boundary claim while leaving the $5,364.44 damages award undisturbed. It sent the case back to the trial court for further proceedings and did not retain jurisdiction. The dispute over the property's boundary will now be considered again by the lower court.
Article Summary: Frederick G. Bender and his wife, Susan, said their family had maintained the 0.13-acre area for years, although it was part of his brother David A. Bender's property. In 2022, David and Jean ploughed the disputed area. They also damaged a separate strip belonging to Frederick and Susan. The couple then filed a lawsuit seeking compensation for the damage and recognition of their claim over the disputed land. An appeals court revived their boundary claim after a lower court rejected it.

Article Title: Bengaluru road rage: Man follows woman to her friend’s apartment, attacks her with bucket
Article Text:
30-year-old woman named Meena experienced a violent attack in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver (AI image)





BENGALURU: A narrow escape from a road accident turned into a terrifying ordeal for a 30-year-old woman in Banashankari when a scooter-borne man, whom she had confronted for driving on the wrong side, allegedly chased her to friend’s apartment and launched a vicious attack. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses.According to the complaint filed by Meena (name changed), a research scholar and resident of Banashankari 3rd Stage, the incident occurred at 10am on Oct 30. She had gone for a workout at a gym and was riding her scooter towards her friend’s apartment when the incident unfolded.On the way, a man riding a scooter with a woman as pillion allegedly approached at high speed from the wrong direction and nearly rammed into her vehicle. Meena narrowly avoided the collision and questioned him over his reckless driving. After the argument, Meena continued towards her friend’s apartment. However, the man allegedly followed her. Even after she reached the apartment and parked her scooter outside, he approached her and assaulted her.She told him not to come near her and rushed inside the apartment. Carrying a bag containing an object, he followed her inside. He attacked her several times on the head, shoulder, arm and forearm, leaving her injured.Even as the man’s wife reportedly tried to restrain him, he picked up an empty paint bucket and struck Meena on the face and neck. The commotion eventually drew the attention of residents and Meena’s friend, who rushed to the spot around 10.15am and questioned the man about his actions. He then stopped the attack and left the apartment complex.Traumatised by the incident, Meena sought medical treatment and filed a complaint on Nov 3.Channammanakere Achukattu police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman), 118 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace).An officer said CCTV footage from the locations where the accused allegedly followed Meena and from the apartment complex was being examined.
Article Summary: 30-year-old woman attacked in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses. Police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace)

Article Text:
A bomb threat email was sent to the Bombay High Court, raising security concerns across Mumbai.





MUMBAI: A bomb threat email was reportedly received targeting the Bombay High Court in Maharashtra, triggering concern over the security of prominent establishments in the city.The email also reportedly named several high-profile locations, including the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Mahalaxmi Racecourse and Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan ’s bungalow, Jalsa.Further details regarding the contents of the email, the credibility of the threat and the action taken by the authorities are awaited.

Article Title: 76-year-old woman’s gold chain snatched by man posing as delivery agent in Mumbai’s Kandivali
Article Text:
An unidentified man impersonating a delivery agent targeted a senior citizen in Mumbai's Kandivali area.





MUMBAI: An unidentified man allegedly posing as a delivery agent snatched the gold chain of a 76-year-old woman inside a residential society in Mumbai’s Kandivali area, police said on Friday.The incident took place on Tuesday night when the victim, Aruna Anilkant Rupani, was standing near the elevator outside her flat at Uman Society on Mathuradas Extension Road.CCTV footage from the society, which has since gone viral on social media, shows the accused approaching Rupani and repeatedly asking her for what appears to be an address.As the senior citizen turns towards her flat, the man suddenly attempts to snatch her gold chain. Despite her resistance, he manages to flee with it.Senior Inspector Karan Kawale of Kandivali police station said a case has been registered and efforts are underway to identify and trace the accused.
Article Summary: Incident took place on Tuesday night when the victim, Aruna Anilkant Rupani, was standing near the elevator outside her flat at Uman Society on Mathuradas Extension Road.CCTV footage from the society, which has since gone viral on social media, shows the accused approaching her.

Article Title: India’s only floating post office in Kashmir’s Dal Lake gets longer working hours
Article Text:
According to officials, it is India's only floating post office. T





SRINAGAR: The Department of Posts today said that it has extended the working hours of the iconic Floating Post Office at Nehru Park in Dal Lake, Srinagar, which will now remain operational from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.The initiative follows the encouraging public response, the department’s spokesperson said.Chief Postmaster General, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, Col. Sagar Hanuman Singh, visited the floating post office today reviewing the facilities. He also interacted with customers, tourists and members of the public to understand their requirements.“Considering the considerable footfall at Nehru Park and the demand for postal services beyond regular office hours, the decision was taken to extend the working hours of the facility,” Singh said, adding that the decision aims to provide greater convenience to customers, tourists and the local population.He said the Department of Posts’ commitment to making postal services more accessible, customer-friendly and responsive to public needs.Officials say that the initiative reflects the Department’s continued efforts to improve service delivery and provide greater flexibility in accessing postal facilities. They said the Floating Post Office is not only an important postal facility but also a distinctive attraction for tourists visiting Kashmir.The extended hours will enable local residents, tourists, houseboat operators and other visitors to access postal services at more convenient times, they added.The story of this post office began in 1953, when a simple postal boat started serving the communities living on Dal Lake making it a vital link between the houseboats and the city. In 2011, it was officially renamed the Floating Post Office, an idea introduced by John Samuel, then Postmaster General of the Jammu and Kashmir Circle.After renovation, the houseboat reopened to the public, drawing interest from both locals and travellers.According to officials, it is India's only floating post office. The office has a unique museum showing rare stamps and postcards portraying the history of the postal service in Jammu and Kashmir. Most of its collection was severely damaged in 2014 devastating floods in the Valley.
Article Summary: The Department of Posts has extended the working hours of the iconic Floating Post Office at Nehru Park in Dal Lake, Srinagar. The initiative follows the encouraging public response, the department’s spokesperson said. Chief Postmaster General, Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, Col. Sagar Hanuman Singh visited the floating post office today reviewing the facilities.

Article Title: Gujarat sugar mill tragedy: 2 killed as hot, cold water tanks collapse
Article Text:
The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.

(With agency inputs)





TAPI: Two employees were killed after hot and cold water tanks collapsed at the Copper Sugar Mill in Dadariya village of Gujarat’s Tapi district, trapping them beneath the debris, officials said on Friday.Following the collapse, police personnel and fire teams from Vyara and Bardoli rushed to the site and launched a rescue operation.After nearly five to six hours of search and rescue efforts, the teams recovered the bodies of both employees from beneath the debris and handed them over to the police.The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.The incident took place around 6:45 pm on Thursday at the sugar mill in Valod taluka.Dilip Odedara of the Vyara Fire Department told news agency ANI that the department received information about the collapse from the Bardoli Fire Control Room and immediately dispatched a team to the site."This incident occurred yesterday evening; around 6:45 PM, we received information from the Bardoli Fire Control Room that a structural collapse had taken place at a sugar factory near Valod. A hot water tank and a cold water tank had collapsed, prompting our deployment to the site," Odedara said.He further said, "After a search operation lasting about 4 to 5 hours, we recovered two bodies and handed them over to the police department."
Article Summary: Two employees were killed after hot and cold water tanks collapsed at the Copper Sugar Mill in Dadariya village of Gujarat’s Tapi district. The deceased have been identified as Arun Patel (54) and Dharmesh Patel (30), both employees of the sugar mill.

Article Title: BSF officer's 28-year-old son dies after falling from 10th floor of Gurgaon society
Article Text:
According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the BSF. (Image-Social Media)





GURGAON: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building at The Leaf Society in Sector 85 on Wednesday morning. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation.According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force (BSF). His father resides at Asia House on KG Marg in Delhi and is currently posted in Koraput, Odisha. The victim lived with his mother in a 10th-floor apartment in one of the towers at The Leaf Society. He was unmarried.Police said Ashim was generally quiet and had no known disputes with anyone. However, he was suspected to have been under mental distress for the past few days and rarely stepped out of his room.The family told police that Ashim was on the balcony on Wednesday morning when he fell. Hearing the noise, family members and other society residents rushed to the spot and took him to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead.Police from Kherki Daula police station reached the spot after receiving information and inspected the scene, including the balcony and the apartment.Police are investigating whether Ashim died by suicide or fell accidentally. Statements are being recorded from family members and other residents, while CCTV footage from the society is also being examined to establish the sequence of events.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old man, identified as Ashim, died after falling from the 10th floor of an apartment building. The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, and police have initiated an investigation. According to police, Ashim was the son of Satyawan Khachi, a senior officer in the Border Security Force.

Article Title: Panchkula school assault case: 8-year-old granted bail; parents barred from giving him mobile phone
Article Text:
The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case (File photo)





PANCHKULA: The Juvenile Justice Board (JJB), Panchkula, has granted bail to the eight-year-old boy facing proceedings in the school assault case after his parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.The Class III student was represented before the board through his father.In the bail application, the parents undertook to take full responsibility for his care and supervision, while ensuring a healthy family environment, proper upbringing, education and moral guidance.They also assured the board that the child would undergo counselling, behavioural intervention and rehabilitation measures as advised by the competent authority.In addition, they undertook to provide him with appropriate medical care and all necessary support for his physical and mental well-being.The application stated that the child had cooperated with investigators and had no previous criminal record.It further argued that prolonged stay in custody could adversely affect his education, academic progress and overall development.The parents also assured the Board that they would ensure his presence whenever required and comply with all conditions imposed while granting bail.In a separate plea filed under Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, the boy’s father sought directions for the removal of videos, photographs and other content related to the case from social media platforms and public forums.The plea contended that such material could lead to the identification of the child and expose him to humiliation, discrimination and bullying.It also sought directions to the investigating officer and school authorities to prevent the further circulation of any material that could reveal the child’s identity.Acting on the application, the board directed authorities to ensure the removal of the assault video from social media within 15 days. The child had earlier been lodged in an observation home in Ambala.The board also directed that his studies should not be disrupted and ordered treatment after receiving a report from GMCH-32, which had recommended medical intervention after observing behavioural abnormalities.The matter is being pursued against the boy under Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing simple hurt), 117(2) (voluntarily causing grievous hurt) and 127(2) (wrongful confinement) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The case was recorded through a Daily Diary Report (DDR) at Sector 20 police station.
Article Summary: The Juvenile Justice Board in Panchkula has granted bail to an eight-year-old boy involved in a school assault case. His parents gave an undertaking that he would not be allowed access to a mobile phone and would undergo counselling, behavioural guidance and any treatment deemed necessary.

Article Title: Bengaluru man beats daughter’s boyfriend to death after catching them together at home
Article Text:
The accused, identified as Anand





BENGALURU: A 22-year-old man from Kerala was allegedly beaten to death in Bengaluru after his girlfriend’s father caught him with his 19-year-old daughter at their house.The accused, identified as Anand, has been arrested.The deceased, Kiran, was a native of Thiruvegappura in Kerala’s Palakkad district.He was reportedly in a relationship with Anand’s daughter and also worked for him.Anand allegedly found the two together at his house and, in a fit of rage, assaulted Kiran. The injuries sustained in the attack led to his death.Anand, who is originally from Tamil Nadu and a native of Yelahanka, runs a company that manufactures machines used for preparing sweet corn. Police have taken him into custody and are investigating the case.
