Article Title: Amid protest by wife, Bihar government transfers IPS officer Bhanu Pratap Singh
Article Text:
Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification (Photo credit: X)





PATNA: The Home department on Wednesday transferred Khagaria SP Bhanu Pratap Singh and called him to police headquarters following days of protest by his wife, Pooja Singh, near the CM’s residence and outside the SP’s official residence, demanding that her family be reunited.The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one in an administrative reshuffle announced on Wednesday evening.According to the transfer order, Shailendra Singh, who was serving as SP in Sheohar, has been transferred to Khagaria as the new SP.Mohibullah Ansari has been shifted from Muzaffarpur City SP to Sheohar SP, while IPS officer Kumari Mamta has been given the additional charge of BMP-16.Pooja had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. On Nov 3, she moved her protest to outside the Khagaria SP’s official residence, reiterating her demand to reunite with her husband and daughter.According to Pooja, she married Bhanu in 2016 in a love marriage, when he was living in Delhi and preparing for the UPSC examination without a job.Puja alleged that she worked as a teacher at a private school to support the household expenses and financially helped her husband during his preparation.She said Bhanu subsequently cleared the UPSC examination and became an IPS officer of the 2021-batch.Pooja alleged that her husband’s behaviour changed after he joined the IPS and that their relationship had been strained for several months.She further claimed that she had not been allowed to meet their six-year-old daughter for the past eight to nine months. “I do not want to separate from my husband, nor do I want to initiate any legal dispute. I only want my family to be together again,” she had said.Pooja said she had repeatedly approached officials seeking intervention in the matter but had not been able to resolve the dispute. Her central demand, she maintained, was to reunite with her husband and daughter and rebuild their family life.Home department’s transfer order came against the backdrop of her protests. However, the order does not specify whether the transfers are directly linked to the domestic dispute.
Article Summary: Bhanu Pratap Singh was transferred from his position as Khagaria SP after his wife protested for family reunification. Pooja Singh had staged a sit-in near the CM’s residence on Nov 1, seeking intervention to save her marriage. The department also transferred three other IPS officers and gave additional charge to one.

Article Title: Smoking, bike rally, songs: Man accused of murdering 16-year-old boy gets hero's welcome after bail
Article Text:
Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail.





SATNA: A man accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy in Madhya Pradesh's Satna district allegedly staged a show of strength on the streets shortly after being released on bail after spending around 14 months in jail.The accused, identified as Man Singh alias Betu Singraul, was welcomed with garlands outside the jail before his supporters took out a bike rally. A video showing him sitting on the bonnet of a Bolero SUV and smoking a cigarette during the procession has gone viral on social media.The rally was reportedly taken out from the jail to Siddharth Colony, with several supporters joining the procession on motorcycles and in vehicles. The incident has raised questions over law and order and whether traffic rules were flouted during the procession.Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown under the jurisdiction of Kolgawan police station, during which a gunshot was allegedly fired. Satyam was shot in the chest during the altercation. He was rushed to hospital but died while being taken to Rewa for treatment.Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail. However, his grand welcome outside the prison and the subsequent procession have triggered controversy.The viral video has also raised questions about the alleged violation of traffic rules and the possibility of public intimidation during the procession. It remains to be seen whether Satna police will take action over the incident.While bail is a legal right, the incident has brought the conduct of the accused and his supporters on public roads under scrutiny.
Article Summary: Man Singh is an accused in the murder of 16-year-old Satyam Shukla. On September 4, a dispute broke out near the FCI godown. Man Singh and other accused were subsequently arrested and lodged in jail. After spending around 14 months behind bars, Man Singh was granted bail.

Article Title: 2 dead in Chawri Bazaar building collapse: MCD suspends assistant engineer, junior engineer over negligence; FIR ordered against contractor
Article Text:
3-storey building collapses in Delhi's Chawri Bazaar

What happened at Gali Sitara?

No building plan sanctioned: MCD





NEW DELHI: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has suspended an assistant engineer and a junior engineer following the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar, which killed two people and injured four others on Thursday.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has also ordered an inquiry into the incident and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor.The action against the MCD officials was taken after the Deputy Commissioner of the Old Delhi Zone found a prima facie case of serious negligence in the discharge of their duties.The suspended officials have been identified as Assistant Engineer (Building) Mohd Naeem and Junior Engineer (Building) Aman Dalal.In separate office orders, the Deputy Commissioner placed both officials under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry.“In view of the recent incident and the developments arising therefrom, and considering the prima facie case of severe dereliction of duty, you are hereby placed under suspension with immediate effect, pending further inquiry,” the orders stated.The three-storey building under construction collapsed in Gali Sitara, near Chawri Bazaar Metro station, around 9.50am on Thursday.More people were initially feared trapped under the debris, officials said.Two people were killed after being trapped under the rubble. A Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team pulled out two bodies from the debris, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by local residents before the fire department teams arrived.The identities of the deceased are yet to be established, police said. Multiple teams, including personnel from the Delhi Fire Services, were deployed to carry out rescue operations.A senior MCD official said the plot on which the three-storey building collapsed measured 50 square metres.No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, and the civic body had not received any complaints regarding its construction.The official said the building was still under construction, although work had been stopped around 15 days before the collapse.According to officials, workers were removing the support system beneath the roof when the building collapsed.The construction material used was non-engineered and had not set properly, which may have contributed to the collapse, they said.(Wiith agency inputs)
Article Summary: Three-storey building under construction collapses in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazaar. Two people killed after being trapped under the rubble. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta has ordered an inquiry into the incident. No building plan had been sanctioned for the structure, civic body says.

Article Title: Pentagon CTO Emil Michael: We helped Ukrainians a ton fighting Russia, but they invented the technology they actually needed because we didn’t have it and it is ...
Article Text:
Pentagon CTO: We were caught flat-footed

Stockpile growth, but Ukraine far ahead

Pentagon studying future battlefields

Cautious on AI targeting

Reiterates criticism of Anthropic

US still ahead of China in AI

The Pentagon’s technology chief Emil Michael has said the United States was unprepared for the rise of modern drone warfare and admitted that Ukraine had to develop some of the battlefield technologies it needed because the US could not provide them. Speaking at the WSJ Tech Conference, Michael said the conflict between Ukraine and Russia exposed significant gaps in America's military preparedness and accelerated efforts to expand the country's drone capabilities.Addressing the conference in Napa, California, Michael said the Pentagon had not anticipated how central drones would become to modern warfare. "We were caught flat-footed by the drone warfare in Ukraine and Russia," he said, adding that the US was not prepared because it "just didn't imagine it." He said the Defence Department is now focused on preparing for future conflicts and anticipating how warfare could evolve.Michael acknowledged that while the United States provided substantial support to Ukraine during its war with Russia, Ukrainian forces often had to create their own solutions on the battlefield. "We helped the Ukrainians a ton, but they invented what they actually needed because we didn't have it," he said.Michael said the US built about 1,000 drones under the previous administration, while its stockpile is now around 500,000. That is still a small fraction of the eight million to 10 million drones Ukraine estimates it will build this year, as its war with Russia nears a fifth year. Michael said the US helped Ukraine a great deal, but Ukrainian forces invented the technology they needed because the US did not have it.Michael said the Defence Department's Project Meridian has been tasked with examining what future warfare could look like, including potential conflicts underground and in space. The initiative includes participation from industry figures such as Elon Musk, chief executive of SpaceX, and Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril IndustriesEven as the Pentagon pushes into cheap, autonomous systems, Michael said the military remains conservative about using artificial intelligence in combat. Developing targets still depends more on intelligence reports, satellite imagery and other human-led investigation than on AI, he said, adding that the US is not very sophisticated at AI-generated targeting.Michael declined to comment on the US strike in Iran last February that hit a girls’ school the US had mistaken for a military target. More than 100 people were killed, including dozens of children. The US has not released the findings of its investigation, and planning for the strike involved an AI targeting system. Michael said there must be appropriate human judgment at every level.Michael also reiterated his criticism of AI company Anthropic, which the Defence Department earlier designated as a national security threat. He said it was not difficult for the Pentagon to stop using Anthropic's models and noted that the department continues to use AI models from Google, OpenAI and Grok on its networks.On the global AI race, Michael argued that the United States maintains an advantage over China thanks to its access to advanced semiconductors and greater data-centre capacity.According to Michael, Beijing remains approximately six months to a year behind the United States in AI development, although he indicated that competition between the two countries remains intense.
Article Summary: Pentagon CTO: We were caught flat-footed by the drone warfare in Ukraine and Russia. He admitted that Ukraine had to develop some of the battlefield technologies it needed because the US could not provide them. Michael said the Pentagon had not anticipated how central drones would become to modern warfare.

Article Title: '36 missiles, 172 drones': Russia to join US-Ukraine talks after massive overnight strikes on Kyiv energy sites
Article Text:
Rescue operations on after Russian strike on Ukraine

Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv and surrounding regions, even as Moscow prepares to join trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine next week.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said all 36 missiles were directed at Kyiv and the surrounding region, with energy facilities bearing the brunt of the attacks. The strikes also damaged residential buildings, the Northern Bridge and a kindergarten, while disrupting electricity, water and heating supplies in the capital.A substation connecting the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine was hit in the Kyiv region. Other substations were damaged in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipro. Twelve regions, apart from Kyiv, came under attack, leaving nine people injured, including a child, Zelenskyy said."Russia is preparing for trilateral talks by launching ballistic missiles at Ukraine’s critical infrastructure," Zelenskyy said, adding that repair and rescue operations were underway wherever the security situation allowed.He also called on the United States to increase bilateral support and maintain Ukraine among its policy priorities.Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax that Russia's delegation for the talks with the US and Ukraine would include senior military officials and diplomats.The meeting is scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday and will be the first trilateral engagement of its kind since February.The Russian delegation will again be led by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky and include deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov, who will join the negotiations for the first time, along with senior General Staff officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky.Deputy foreign minister Mikhail Galuzin and military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov are also expected to participate.Russian President Vladimir Putin met the delegation at a security council meeting on Friday to discuss preparations for the talks. He thanked the United Arab Emirates for hosting the negotiations.
Article Summary: Russia launched 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones at Ukraine overnight, targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv and surrounding regions. Moscow prepares to join trilateral talks with the United States and Ukraine next week. The meeting is scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday and will be the first trilateral engagement of its kind since February.

Article Title: 36 lives lost to house collapses this year in Delhi
Article Text:
A similar pattern of alleged negligence emerged in the Sept 6 collapse in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, including five students and two labourers.





NEW DELHI: From crumbling houses to collapsing structures, a series of incidents across Delhi has raised a pressing question: how safe are the buildings people live and work in?Delhi Fire Service data paints a worrying picture, with 36 deaths reported in house-collapse incidents from Jan to Oct 2026.The data says that the fire department received 396 calls related to house collapses till Oct 26. While 36 people lost their lives, 139 were rescued.According to a fire department official, faulty construction and structural weaknesses were the main contributors to the collapses.The situation was no different in 2025. The department received more than 500 calls related to house collapses, in which over 50 people died and more than 170 were rescued.Investigations into a series of building collapse incidents have repeatedly pointed to construction-related negligence, unauthorised modifications and violations of building safety norms.In May, the collapse of a five-storey building in Saidulajab, which claimed six lives, was attributed to multiple violations, including the construction of unauthorised additional floors, the use of substandard building materials and disregard for mandatory building safety norms, according to the inquiry.A similar pattern of alleged negligence emerged in the Sept 6 collapse in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan, which killed seven people, including five students and two labourers.The inquiry found that a wall on the ground floor, which was obstructing space earmarked for a shop, was removed to create additional space without obtaining the necessary approval from any competent authority. The building subsequently collapsed.According to officials, several factors could contribute to building collapses, particularly in older structures.One of the major reasons, they explained, is the addition of floors to buildings without assessing whether their existing foundations and structural framework can bear the increased load."Many old buildings were constructed with foundations designed to support only the original structure. Over the years, additional floors are added, increasing the load on the foundation beyond its capacity. In many cases, the foundation is simply not equipped to withstand this additional weight, which can weaken the structure and eventually lead to a collapse," said Atul Garg, former director of Delhi Fire Service.He also pointed to the risks associated with construction and renovation work in and around existing buildings.The use of heavy machinery during such activities generates vibrations and causes repeated jerks, which can affect the structural stability of adjoining or already weakened buildings.
Article Summary: Delhi Fire Service data paints a worrying picture, with 36 deaths reported in house-collapse incidents from Jan to Oct 2026. The fire department received 396 calls related to house collapses till Oct 26. While 36 people lost their lives, 139 were rescued. According to a fire department official, faulty construction and structural weaknesses were the main contributors to the collapses.

Article Title: Four hurt in JNU hostel clash with cleaver over girl
Article Text:
A violent altercation between two JNU students occurred over a woman friend, resulting in serious injuries (File Photo)





NEW DELHI: A quarrel between two JNU students over a woman friend turned violent when one of them allegedly attacked the other with a butcher's knife inside Barak Hostel on the university campus on Thursday, reports Sugandha Jha."Two students started fighting over a female friend. During the fight, one student took out a butcher's knife and attacked the other on the face, causing serious injuries, including to his eyes," said JNU security officer Naveen Yadav. The alleged attacker was also injured. The 19-year-old woman at the centre of the dispute and a fourth student were also injured. "All the injured students were admitted to AIIMS Trauma Centre," Yadav said.Police have registered a case of attempt to murder.No arrest has been made so far as the alleged attacker is also hospitalised,” an officer said.The university has submitted a report to the chief proctor’s office and is expected to take further action based on the FIR.According to police and JNU, all four injured persons were students. However, the AIIMS statement referred to the involvement of 10 people in the violence, indicating that the violence, which broke out inside a room, swelled into a group clash.“A 22-year-old male patient, whose case record mentions an assault involving 10 people, suffered serious injuries to his right eye, nose, face and shoulders, along with multiple fractures. He underwent surgery,” said Rima Dada, media cell in-charge of AIIMS.“The 19-year-old woman, who was reportedly physically assaulted by two known people, suffered cuts and wounds on her forearm and hand that required stitches. A 24-year-old man suffered injuries to his wrist and fingers, including tendon damage, and underwent surgery. A fourth patient, a 39-year-old man, was reportedly assaulted by 10 people,” AIIMS added.
Article Summary: A quarrel between two JNU students over a woman friend turned violent when one of them allegedly attacked the other with a butcher's knife. The 19-year-old woman at the centre of the dispute and a fourth student were also injured. All the injured students were admitted to AIIMS Trauma Centre.

Article Title: 3 contractors held over Delhi building collapse
Article Text:
A building collapse in Chawri Bazar, Delhi, led to the deaths of two labourers, Kishori Sah and Sanjeet.

TOI





NEW DELHI: A day after a building collapse in central Delhi's Chawri Bazar claimed two lives, police apprehended three contractors from Sirohi village in Faridabad district Friday. They were arrested later.Siraj, Tajuddin and Furkan were arrested in a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the collapse. "The contractors knew that such an incident could happen, but they didn't pay any heed," an officer said, adding that no safety equipment was given to workers.A senior officer said the contractors were involved in arranging labourers for the construction, which was being carried out late at night despite anti-pollution restrictions under Graded Response Action Plan.The accused were aware that they did not have the requisite permissions to carry out construction work and had not got the building plan approved by the authority, he added.The officer also said that though the contractors were not physically present at the site when the incident occurred Thursday morning, they were aware of the collapse through telephone calls. They allegedly fled after switching off their mobile phones.According to police, Siraj and Taj­uddin are residents of Gali Sitara in the Ajmeri Gate area, while Furkan lives in Gali Nal Wali in Ajmeri Gate’s Sha­hganj Chowk.Police sources toldthat the construction of the four-storey residential building had been under way for the past four to five months. “We suspect that the construction was not carried out properly. They were adding more floors, but the foundation may not have been strong enough to bear the additional load, leading to the collapse,” they added.According to preliminary information, four people were rescued from the debris. Two of them succumbed to their injuries, while the other two are reported to be stable. The deceased labourers were identified as Kishori Sah (40) and Sanjeet (45), both residents of Railway Colony in Mandawali. The injured have been identified as Sahdev Chaudhary (25) and Firoz (37). They are residents of Mandawali and Railway Colony, respectively.The rescue operation is still on, but nobody was found Friday, said sources.
Article Summary: Three contractors from Sirohi village in Faridabad district were arrested later. Siraj, Tajuddin and Furkan were arrested in a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the collapse. The contractors knew that such an incident could happen, but they didn't pay any heed.

Article Title: Man strangles wife after row over students' fathers visiting home, dies by suicide
Article Text:
The deceased have been identified as Majid Khan (50) and his wife Tabassum Khan (41).





NALASOPARA: A 50-year-old man allegedly strangled his wife to death over suspicion about her character before jumping in front of a moving train at Grant Road railway station on Saturday afternoon.The deceased have been identified as Majid Khan (50) and his wife Tabassum Khan (41). The couple lived in Takipada, Nalasopara West.According to the police, Tabassum conducted tuition classes at home.Majid reportedly suspected her character because the fathers of her students would visit their house. This often led to arguments between the couple.On Saturday around 5am, Majid allegedly strangled Tabassum to death following another argument over the same issue. He then left the house.Later in the afternoon, he allegedly jumped in front of a moving train at Grant Road railway station, ending his life.Nalasopara police are investigating the incident.
Article Summary: The deceased have been identified as Majid Khan (50) and his wife Tabassum Khan (41) The couple lived in Takipada, Nalasopara West. Majid reportedly suspected her character because the fathers of her students would visit their house. This often led to arguments between the couple.

Article Title: BEST files police complaint over ‘missing’ bus stop after Sena MLA rebuilds shelter in Mumbai's Andheri
Article Text:
BEST recently filed a police complaint about a missing bus shelter in Andheri, which had been rebuilt





MUMBAI: It's not every day that a police complaint is filed over a missing bus stop. Public transport undertaking BEST did exactly that after a newly rebuilt bus shelter in Andheri (E) by Shiv Sena MLA Murji Patel set off a controversy over permissions, public assets and the disappearance of the original structure.Shiv Sena (UBT) member Sachin Patil questioned the legitimacy of the shelter at Shree Andheri KVO Seva Samaj Chowk on Old Nagardas Road in Friday's BEST committee meet. The structure displays the BEST logo, signboards crediting Patel (Kaka) for its construction and a list of bus stops. A senior BEST official said they were surprised to find the original shelter missing, and filed a police complaint.BEST has since filed a police “missing complaint” and is seeking details of how the new structure came up. Patil sought to know whether approvals had been obtained from BEST, BMC and traffic authorities, whether a tendering process was followed, who funded the project and who authorised the use of the BEST logo.Patel said, “There is no illegal work here. We have taken proper permissions from the BEST as well as the BMC ward office and the necessary NOCs required to take over the old bus stop and construct the new one.” He said MLA funds were used to revamp the shelter, adding that his name appeared on it because the work was funded from his allocation.He denied any illegality or a “missing bus stop” and said he would respond to queries from the BEST panel or its chairperson, Trushna Vishwasrao, who too is from Sena. Patil said the controversy also raised concerns over ad revenue, which BEST earns through contracts linked to bus shelters. Unauthorised rebuilding or modification of shelters could set a precedent, he said.Vishwasrao assured members she would obtain details by the next meeting. She also ordered inspections of other bus stops modified by political party leaders. BEST GM Sonia Sethi called for verification of whether MLA, MP or other public funds were used. Sena (UBT) member Nitin Nandgaonkar demanded stringent action if an unauthorised takeover was established. “We demand a thorough probe and how the original bus stop went missing,” he said.
Article Summary: BEST has filed a police complaint about a missing bus shelter in Andheri, which had been rebuilt by Shiv Sena MLA Murji Patel. Patel denies any illegality or a ‘missing bus stop’ and said he would respond to queries from the BEST panel.
